title.narrative: Global Coordination Project-Clean and Healthy Ocean Integrated Program

description.narrative: 229. CHO-IP co-benefits include supporting a sustainable blue economy by curbing inflow of land-based-pollution into the coastal environment, thereby advancing the ecological, social, and economic well-being of countries and LMEs. The CHO-IP will help to support livelihoods, better human health, enhance food security and economic well-being and help strengthen resilience to climate change and its impacts, and overall, the CHO-IP will directly contribute to GEF’s “Healthy Planet, Healthy People” framework.230. The GCP supports the CPs in delivering their socio-economic benefits but, like the contribution to GEF Core Indicators, the GCP does not directly contribute major socio-economic benefits itself. The most significant contributions made by the GCP relate to its technical capacity service provision to the CPs, particularly through best management practices (Component 3) and in relation to gender. 231. The GCP will offer support to improve benefits and opportunities to women through a comprehensive Gender Action Plan (GAP, see Annex J) for the CHO-IP, key elements of which will be adopted by all the CPs. The GCP will oversee the implementation of the GAP providing support to CPs to facilitate inclusive gender-responsive policies and incentives to addressing nutrient pollution and marine hypoxia, and by encouraging private sector and social enterprise investment in female-led businesses opportunities (especially through the interventions of the three RMDBs), opening new opportunities for markets and decent employment, particularly in the agricultural sector where women dominate informal employment, and improving participation of women in decision-making in related to activities that cause or mitigate nutrient pollution and marine hypoxia.232. In general terms, the four IA's of the GCP will follow, throughout implementation, the GEF guidance: Key Principles to Strengthen Knowledge Management, Learning, and Interoperability Platforms for GEF Integrated Approach Programs.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To enhance the effectiveness of the CHO IP in addressing nutrient pollution and marine hypoxia by curbing coastal pollution from agriculture, industrial, and municipal sources through gender-responsive policy and regulatory measures, infrastructure investments, nature-based solutions and inclusive awareness-raising initiatives globally, regionally and in participating countries, thereby delivering increased global environmental benefits.
